3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: After a long day at the palace, I was finally home. I thanked Serge and walked through the front gates, nodding at the two guards as I went by.

4.speaker: Monica
4.text: “Deana, what did I tell you? No running in the house.”

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Even as I turned the doorknob, I could hear Deana rushing down the stairs to greet me.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: I lifted Deana up and hugged her while trying to put the keys in the tray next to the entrance.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: She was growing fast. Lifting her up was no longer as easy as it once was.

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “Oof! That's enough of that. You're a big girl now!”

17.speaker: Deana
17.text: “That's right! I'm a big girl now!”

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: I put her down and her expression turned serious.

19.speaker: Deana
19.text: "Boring. I liked my old school better."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: Monica appeared next to the kitchen door. She was wearing an apron and holding a spatula in her hand.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Monica approached me and kissed me on the cheek. A tantalizing smell wafted from the kitchen behind her.

24.speaker: Player
24.text: “Darling, you shouldn't have. What do we have a cook for?"

27.speaker: Monica
27.text: “Terrific. I finally got to do some grocery shopping, just like old times. And I'm making your favorite.”

28.speaker: Monica
28.text: “I felt like going grocery shopping, just like old times. And besides, she can't make your favorite like I can."

29.speaker: Monica
29.text: “Hello to you too, Anton. It's almost done. I'm making your favorite.”

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Zabla was one of my hometown's specialties -- a chickpea stew topped with beef braised in tomatoes and Bergian spices, traditionally served in a clay pot.

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: It was absolutely my favorite dish -- especially paired with Kebij, a potent unfiltered wine from my region.

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “Mmm. It's my lucky day. What's the occasion?”

35.speaker: Monica
35.text: “No occasion. I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."

36.speaker: Monica
36.text: “Especially after what happened at the ball.”

37.speaker: Monica
37.text: "What, you and Petr didn't booze it up enough back at the palace?"

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: Her smile faded, and she lowered her voice so that Deana wouldn't hear.

39.speaker: Monica
39.text: “I am worried, Anton. For you, for the children -- and for the country."

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: Deana suddenly appeared next to us.

44.speaker: Monica
44.text: “We'll eat in just a minute. Will you help me set the table?”

45.speaker: Monica
45.text: “Anton, can you tell Franc to come down for dinner? He's been sulking in his room all day.”

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Monica started taking out the plates while I headed upstairs to fetch my son.

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: Loud rock 'n' roll music echoed down the hallway from his room. I caught a faint hint of cigarette smoke.

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “Franc, turn down that racket and open the door!”

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: The stereo in Franc's room clicked off.

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: He unlocked and opened the door.

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Hand over those cigarettes and join your family for dinner.”

64.speaker: Franc
64.text: “You smoke, don't you? I'm old enough to do what I want!"

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “I am your father and you will respond when I ask for you!”

66.speaker: Franc
66.text: “Sorry, Dad -- I mean, Father. It won't happen again.”

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Franc headed downstairs to the dining room and I followed after.

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: The table was prepared and Monica was ladling food onto the plates.

70.speaker: Monica
70.text: “Come on. Have a seat. It won't be as tasty if it's cold.”

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: As we started eating, the room went quiet. Monica's cooking was as delicious as ever, but I had the feeling that wasn't the reason nobody spoke.

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: Monica was the first to break the silence.

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: Franc suddenly slammed his hands on the table, rattling the plates. Monica, Deana and I stared at him.

74.speaker: Franc
74.text: “So, this is how it's going to be? We're just going to sit here like nothing happened?"

75.speaker: Franc
75.text: "Dad, you could have been killed. Mom could have been killed. Any one of us could have died!"

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “And what would you have us do?”

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “And yet, we are all still alive.”

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “You will not raise your voice to me, young man.”

79.speaker: Franc
79.text: “I don't know. Talk about it. Maybe.”

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: Deana's lower lip started trembling. Monica put her hand on Franc's shoulder.

81.speaker: Franc
81.text: “For now. But how long until this happens again?”

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: Franc got up from his seat.

84.speaker: Franc
84.text: "You don't care! You don't care what happens to me or Deana or anyone else--"

85.speaker: Monica
85.text: “Franc, honey, we can talk about this--”

86.speaker: Franc
86.text: “No, it's too late! Ugh, I hate this family."

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: He stormed out of the dining room. Deana started crying. Monica soothed her for a bit, then plopped her in front of the living room TV and returned to the table.

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: I opened the door and there she was, standing in front of me with expectant eyes.

89.speaker: Monica
89.text: “Say, did you know that they refurbished the grocery store?”

90.speaker: Monica
90.text: “I don't know if you remember the owner -- he's been there every day for the past 30 years.”

91.speaker: Monica
91.text: “Can you imagine doing the same job for so long? What if you were president for 20 years, for example?”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “Honestly, would that really be so bad?"

93.speaker: Player
93.text: “I don't want this country to suffer under another Soll.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “20 years of this? I'd be dead!"

95.speaker: Monica
95.text: “Anyway, the grocer really is a nice person. He threw in some extra vegetables with my--"

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Monica measured me with her eyes for a moment.

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “Fine, let's talk about it. Sit down.”

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "Go, then. And don't even think about coming out until you've learned to show some respect!"

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: Franc took his seat again, scowling.

110.speaker: Player
110.text: “Don't worry. We are going to be fine.”

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “Do you think I would let us go down so easily?”

112.speaker: Player
112.text: “I know it was a close call, but everything is under control.”

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “You don't need to know the details.”

115.speaker: Player
115.text: “My security assured me that they took all the necessary steps.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “It was one rogue shooter. We were not even the target.”

117.speaker: Franc
117.text: “The same security that let a person get shot in front of the palace?”

122.speaker: Franc
122.text: “But it's not up to you, is it?”

123.speaker: Franc
123.text: “How are we possibly going to be fine?”

127.speaker: Monica
127.text: “Franc. Listen to your father. If your father says we don't need to worry, then we don't need to worry.”

129.speaker: Monica
129.text: “We all have to trust each other.”

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: Things calmed down a bit at the table. We finished our food in silence.

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: Had I been lying to Franc and Deana? Was the threat to my family truly over?

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: I sat alone at the table and drained my glass of Kebij.

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: Franc got up first and retreated back to his room. Monica lifted Deana up and plopped her in front of the living room TV before returning to the table.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: She sat down across from me.

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “I promise if there truly is any threat to this family, you will be the first to know.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “All you need to worry about is putting more delicious dinner on our table.”

138.speaker: Player
138.text: “I worry too, Monica. Things might escalate.”

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: She got up, stood behind me and massaged my shoulders for a moment before leaving me alone in the dining room.

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “Why not? We could live like kings.”

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: Monica measured me with her eyes for a moment.

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “Franc. You know I would never let anything happen to you or Deana. Even if it costs me my life.”

149.speaker: Franc
149.text: “Can you at least tell me if something's being done about this? It was real close, dad.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: "It was only one bad man, Deana. And yes, he's gone now."

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "I will never let anyone hurt you, ever."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: "Yes, your papa took care of everything!"

157.speaker: Monica
157.text: "I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."

158.speaker: Monica
158.text: "Anyway, I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: I realized my poor choice of words too late. Monica looked down at her plate.

161.speaker: Monica
161.text: “He's scared, Anton. And frankly, he isn't the only one.”

162.speaker: Monica
162.text: "You make plenty of rash decisions now, too. Franc's not the only one who's scared, Anton."

163.speaker: Player
163.text: "He should feel lucky he has a father who cares about him. I never had that."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "He's had every opportunity I never did. Why is he still acting out?"

166.speaker: Player
166.text: "I know. But there's not much longer we can shield him from the ugliness of the world."

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "My father would've given me hell for that kind of insubordination."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "That's what worries me. I made plenty of rash decisions when I was his age."

175.speaker: Narrator
175.text: Monica frowned at me and left to join Deana.

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: I could have lost my son back at the palace. Maybe he was right to be mad. Was the threat to my family truly over?

182.speaker: Narrator
182.text: It was absolutely my favorite dish -- especially paired with Kebij, a potent unfiltered wine from Bergia.

183.speaker: Player
183.text: “Turn those records up louder next time, won't you? I don't think the neighbors heard.”

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "As long as you live in this house, you'll do as I command!”

186.speaker: Player
186.text: "I'm trying to quit that nasty habit. You ought to stop while you still can.”

187.speaker: Player
187.text: "I'm just asking you to wait until you're out of the house.”

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Franc heaved a sigh, handed me the packet and headed downstairs. I followed him to the living room.

200.speaker: Narrator
200.text: Svabli was a classic Holsord delicacy -- vegetables and creamy sheep cheese sandwiched between thin layers of dough.

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Lorscha was a Lachaven specialty usually reserved for special occasions -- a rich seafood stew with a heady garlic and paprika kick.
